title: Service Guard: cross-functional SLO pilot & experimentation framework
content:
Purpose and high-level summary:

This doc describes the Service Guard pilot: a focused cross-functional program to (1) standardize how teams define and operationalize SLOs for externally visible inference services, (2) run a 6-week experiment to validate an SLO adoption flow and incident choreography, and (3) produce repeatable artifacts (templates, playbooks, dashboards) that other product teams can adopt.

Why now:
- We have multiple ad-hoc SLO efforts across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments; inconsistent measurement and incident escalation increases time-to-recovery and customer confusion.
- Leadership wants a small, evidence-backed program we can scale into an operations playbook for 2027.

Primary goals (quantified where possible):
- Pilot adoption across 2 product services (hosted-api generation route + dedicated routing proxy) within 6 weeks.
- Reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO-breaches by 30% in pilot services within the pilot window.
- Capture and preserve 80% of runbook steps into a canonical SLO playbook and 3 templated dashboards.
- Validate escalation taxonomy with on-call teams and engineering managers (2 tabletop drills).

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: definition of service SLOs, measurement pipelines, alert thresholds, runbooks, oncall choreography, 2 tabletop exercises, dashboards and cost impact analysis.
- Out-of-scope: infra-level kernel/runtime optimization work, billing model changes, company-wide SLA contracts.

Success hypothesis and acceptance criteria:
- Hypothesis: A standardized SLO template + lightweight measurement pipeline will enable feature teams to onboard SLOs with <3 engineer-days of effort and reduce operational toil measured by fewer post-incident action-items.
- Acceptance criteria: both pilot services have an active SLO tracked for 4+ rolling weeks, have at least one successful failover/fallback exercised, and post-pilot retro shows >50% of owners rate the process as "useful" (survey).

Stakeholders and roles (proposed):
- Program lead (owner): Priya Nair (SRE) — coordination, delivery, stakeholder management
- Product leads: Maya Chen (Hosted API), Carlos Rivera (Dedicated) — define product-level intent and map customer impact
- Observability & Metrics: Aisha Patel — dashboards, metric instrumentation, alert plumbing
- Oncall & Runbook SME: Liam O'Connor — incident choreography, escalation matrix, tabletop facilitation
- Solutions Eng / CS liaison: Jordan Park — customer-facing messaging and opt-in list
- Engineering partners: two eng leads per pilot service (names TBD)

Deliverables:
- Standard SLO template (1 page) with guidance on objective selection, measurement, and error budget policy.
- Measurement pipeline guide: end-to-end diagram + required metrics (p99 latency, p95 latency, success-rate, error-rate, tail CPU/mem signals).
- Dashboard kit: Grafana/Datadog dashboard with prebuilt widgets and thresholds.
- Runbook cookbook: playbook steps for breach detection, mitigation, rollback, and postmortem checklist.
- Tabletop drill plan and artifact (scripting + recording) for two scenarios.
- Pilot retro and adoption decision doc.

High-level timeline (6-week pilot):
- Week 0: Kickoff, stakeholder alignment, finalize services, agree success metrics
- Week 1: Instrumentation and metric gaps discovery; create SLO templates for both services
- Week 2: Implement metric collection & dashboards; validate data quality (slo-quality check)
- Week 3: Define error budget policy and alerting thresholds; publish runbooks draft
- Week 4: Tabletop exercise 1 (hosted-api) and iterate runbook; mitigation play tested
- Week 5: Tabletop exercise 2 (dedicated proxy); collect feedback; adjust dashboards & alerts
- Week 6: Post-pilot retro, adoption decision, handoff to product/platform ops

Swimlanes (Who does what):
- SRE Program (Priya): coordinate, template authoring, runbooks consolidation
- Observability (Aisha): metric plumbing, dashboards, alerts, data quality checks
- Product Eng (Maya/Carlos): service-specific SLO intent, implement labeling/metrics at service boundary
- Oncall Owners (Liam + service oncall): validate escalation, participate in tabletop drills
- Solutions/CS: customer comms, optional early adopter cohort management

Instrumentation checklist (notes to implementers):
- Ensure requests are tagged with route and customer tier labels at ingress.
- Export latency histograms with p50/p95/p99 buckets and request outcome (success, reject, error).
content_continued:
- Export a boolean success metric for per-request reliability (true = acceptable response returned).
- Ensure sampling of KV-cache hit rate and fallback counts (important for cost/latency tradeoffs).
- Add synthetic traffic generator for tabletop tests (small harness that can run sequences to cause throttles/fallbacks).

Alerting and policy guidance:
- Two alert tiers: (A) imminent error-budget burn (e.g., 25% burn in 1 hour), (B) sustained breach (error rate above threshold for >1 hour).
- Alert routing: Tier A -> service oncall + SRE program; Tier B -> ENG oncall + product lead + escalation to duty manager.
- Auto-actions: annotate incidents with runbook link and auto-populate incident template.

Tabletop exercise scenarios (examples):
1) Gradual capacity degradation: upstream quantization change causes p99 latency to drift upward; error budget burn triggers alerts and fallback routing needs to be validated.
2) Region outage + traffic surge: failover to another region causes cache misses and spike in latency. Focus on rollback, capacity rebalancing, and customer comms.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: instrumentation gaps lead to false signals -> Mitigation: data-quality checklist and at least one ‘golden query’ per metric
- Risk: too many noisy alerts -> Mitigation: harden thresholds in staging, optional suppression window during drill
- Risk: teams perceive this as extra compliance work -> Mitigation: emphasize quick wins (template, dashboards) and measure onboarding time saved

Post-pilot artifacts and handoff:
- Handoff checklist to product/platform ops: canonical SLO template, dashboards, runbook, incident report of drills, lessons learned doc
- Recommended retention: keep pilot dashboards & runbooks in shared drive for 12 months; link in product onboarding repo

Survey & feedback plan:
- Quick pulse after each tabletop: 5 question survey (usefulness, clarity, effort to implement, confidence in oncall, open comments)
- Final survey: adoption intent, suggested tweaks, estimate of ongoing weekly overhead

Decision points to resolve in kickoff meeting (open items):
- Which specific service routes will be used as canonical for hosted-api? (shortlist: /v1/generate/text, /v1/chat/stream)
- Agreement on error budget burn windows (1h vs 3h sensitivity)
- Whether to include a billing-cost signal in SLOs or keep purely reliability-focused

Mini checklist for kickoff (Priya):
- Confirm pilot services and eng leads by EOD Fri
- Reserve two 90-min slots for tabletop drills (weeks 4 and 5)
- Provision staging dashboard spaces and synthetic traffic harness
- Create initial Confluence page and link to this doc

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Keep runbook language simple; engineers will copy paste.
- Try a single-file SLO manifest (YAML) that can be parsed to auto-generate dashboard + alerts (long-term automation).
- Capture command snippets for chaos/synthetic harness in a repo example.

Appendix: quick SLO template (one-liner items)
- Service name:
- Owner(s):
- Customer-facing intent (1 sentence):
- Measurement definition (metric and aggregation):
- Target objective (e.g., 99.5% request success over 30d):
- Error budget policy (burn action at 25/50/90%):
- Primary alert(s):
- Fallback/mitigation options:
- Playbook link:

Next steps (immediate):
- Send kickoff invite to stakeholders (Priya) + add agenda
- Product leads confirm routes and provide labeling plan
- Observability run gap analysis and provide initial dashboard wireframes by end of week 1

-- end --
